chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskān, from Zurārah, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:
The divorced woman inherits and is inherited from until she sees the third menses; when she sees it, the connection is severed.
ai.seo_question: How long does a divorced woman remain in the state of marriage regarding inheritance?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam clarifies the 'iddah of a divorced woman by linking the legal severance of the marital bond to the observation of three menstrual cycles, a ruling derived from the Imams (peace be upon them). It underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the continuity of inheritance rights during 'iddah serves as a tangible indicator of the ongoing marital status until the specified physical sign appears. This narration is pivotal in distinguishing between the waiting period for menstruating women and those with irregular or absent cycles, ensuring precise application of inheritance laws.
